stimulus.body: Doverstone discovers that a supplier uses a cheap accounting software process that harms local water, cutting costs by $39,400 a year. Publicly disclosing the issue would raise costs but protect the community.

questions.stem: Doverstone, which response best aligns with corporate social responsibility?

options.text: Switch suppliers only if regulators threaten a fine
options.misconception: Makes ethical action contingent on external enforcement

options.text: Blame the supplier publicly while continuing to buy from them
options.misconception: Substitutes a reputational gesture for corrective action

options.text: Keep the arrangement quiet because lower costs benefit shareholders
options.misconception: Treats profit maximization as overriding all social concerns

options.text: Disclose the problem and work with the supplier to adopt a cleaner process

questions.explanation: Corporate social responsibility means voluntarily accounting for social and environmental effects, not merely obeying laws or chasing profit. Disclosing the harm and remediating it addresses the community impact while preserving the business relationship.
questions.hint: Look for the option that accepts short-term cost to fix real harm.
